blocks.raw:
<ComparisonTable>

| Group | Description | Typical Building Types |
|---|---|---|
| **Group 1** | Buildings of the simplest utilization and character | Armories, bakeries, freight facilities, hangars, industrial plants, manufacturing plants, warehouses, parking structures, public markets, service garages |
| **Group 2** | Buildings of moderate complexity of plan/design | Art galleries, banks, call centers, churches, colleges, dormitories, exhibition halls, libraries, malls, motels, nursing homes, office buildings, residential condominiums, restaurants, schools, shopping centers, supermarkets |
| **Group 3** | Buildings of exceptional character and complexity | Airports, aquariums, auditoriums, breweries, convention facilities, gymnasiums, hospitals, hotels, laboratories, marinas, mental institutions, research facilities, stadia, theaters, transportation facilities, veterinary hospitals |
| **Group 4** | Residences | Single-detached, single-attached, duplex, row-houses, shop-houses, small apartment houses, townhouses |
| **Group 5** | Monumental buildings | Exposition/fair buildings, museums, mausoleums, memorials, specialized decorative buildings |
| **Group 6** | Repetitive construction | Projects where plans/designs and Contract Documents are **re-used** for the repetitive construction of similar buildings without amending drawings and specifications |
| **Group 7** | Housing projects | Construction of several residential units on a single site using **one basic plan and specifications** |
| **Group 8** | Extensive detail | Designs for built-in components/elements, built-in equipment, special fittings, screens, counters, architectural interiors (AI), development planning and/or design |
| **Group 9** | Alterations/renovations | Alterations, renovations, rehabilitations, retrofits, and expansions/additions to existing buildings belonging to Groups 1 to 5 |
| **Group 10** | Opinion/advice only | The architect is engaged to render opinion, give advice, provide clarifications, or explanations on technical matters pertaining to architectural works |

</ComparisonTable>

| Group | Fee Basis |

| **Group 4** (Residences) | **10%** of Project Construction Cost (flat) |
| **Group 5** (Monumental) | 10% of PCC (requires consummate design skill and precise detailing) |
| **Group 6** (Repetitive) | 1st structure: full basic fee; 2nd: 80% of basic fee; 3rd: 60%; succeeding: 40% |
| **Group 7** (Housing Projects) | 1st unit: 10% of PCC; 2nd–10th: fee of 1st + 60% of basic fee per additional unit; 11th+: fee of 10 units + 30% of basic fee per additional unit |
| **Group 8** (Extensive Detail) | **15%** of Project Construction Cost (flat) |
| **Group 9** (Alterations/Renovations) | **150%** of the applicable Group 1–5 minimum basic fee |

</ComparisonTable>

blocks.raw:
<ComparisonTable>

| Method | Best Used For | Key Feature |
|---|---|---|
| **Percentage of PCC** | All regular building projects (Groups 1–9) | Most common; fee tied to construction cost |
| **MDPE (Multiple of Direct Personnel Expenses)** | Non-creative tasks (research, reports, data gathering) | Multiplier of 1.5–2.5 on direct personnel hours |
| **Professional Fee + Expenses** | Continuing/repeat relationships | Fixed sum + reimbursements |
| **Lump Sum / Fixed Fee** | Government projects; well-defined scope | Predictable total cost |
| **Per Diem + Honorarium** | Short personal-time engagements | Daily rate + out-of-pocket expenses |
| **Mixed Methods** | Complex, multi-phase projects | Combination of above methods |

</ComparisonTable>

<ComparisonTable>

| Preceding / Parallel Document | Relationship |
|---|---|
| **SPP Doc. 201** (Pre-Design Services) | Provides the Architectural Program and feasibility groundwork that feeds Phase 1 of SPP 202 |
| **SPP Doc. 203** (Specialized Services) | Supplements SPP 202 for special areas (interiors, acoustic design, heritage conservation, etc.) — separately contracted and compensated |
| **SPP Doc. 204-A** (Fulltime Supervision) | Engaged when the owner requires 8-hour on-site supervision beyond SPP 202's periodic visits |
| **SPP Doc. 204-B** (Construction Management) | Engaged for broader management responsibilities over the entire construction process |
| **SPP Doc. 205** (Post-Construction) | Takes over after project turnover for building maintenance, administration, and post-occupancy evaluation |
| **SPP Doc. 206** (Comprehensive Services) | Packages SPP 201 through 205 into a single comprehensive engagement |

</ComparisonTable>
